name: Achensee Schifffahrt
kurzbeschreibung: Since 1887, the Achensee boat cruise has connected Tyrol's largest lake: panoramic alpine cruises and scheduled services across six piers.
beschreibung:
Overview

Since 1887, the Achensee Schifffahrt has connected the six landing stages around Tyrol's largest lake, making it one of the oldest passenger shipping companies in Austria. Today, the fleet consists of three modern motor vessels – MS Tirol (1995, approx. 400 seats), MS Stadt Innsbruck (2007, approx. 450 seats), and MS Achensee (2016, approx. 490 seats) – which cruise the entire lake daily with hop-on/hop-off service.

History

The concession was granted on May 22, 1887; on June 27, 1887, the screw steamer St. Josef began scheduled service under the patronage of Fiecht Abbey (Abbot Albert Wildauer). In 1889, the steamer St. Benedikt followed; in 1911, the Stella maris became the very first diesel-powered passenger ship in Austria. Today, Achensee Schifffahrt GmbH has its headquarters at Seepromenade 36 in Pertisau.

Visit & Arrival

Scheduled services run daily from early May to late October between 09:00 and approx. 17:30. Hop-on/hop-off day ticket (2025/26 season): adults €34.00, children 7–15 years €17.00, children up to 6 years free; family day pass €68.00. Combined train & boat ticket (Achenseebahn + round trip cruise): adults €72.00, children €34.50. Traditional Advent cruises take place in winter. Piers: Pertisau (central ticket office), Seespitz/Maurach (connection to Achenseebahn), Buchau (beach lido), Gaisalm (accessible only by boat or lakeside trail), Seehofkapelle/Lido, and Scholastika. By car: A12 exit Wiesing, B181 to Maurach/Pertisau. By public transport: ÖBB to Jenbach, VVT bus line 4080 to Pertisau.

Tips

Modern landing stages are barrier-free; holders of a disability pass (from 50% disability rating) receive a 10% discount including an accompanying person. Dogs are welcome on board with leash and muzzle. The Gaisalm is a rewarding excursion destination – accessible only by boat or via the scenic lakeside path.
